Swole used to be the 'correct' past-tense of 'swell': swell/swole/swollen. Over the centuries that changed to swell/swelled/swollen. "Swole" shows up in literature and poetry from Chaucer and Donne into the 19th century, where "swelled" takes over as the more popular form.

"Swole" survived in US southern dialects -- President Bill Clinton used it a 1999 interview about how his opponents "practically swole up and died" in response to a bill passing. But it seems to have entered the popular vernacular through athletes and rappers. There are a lot of references to someone's eye or knee being "swole up" after a game in sports reportage starting in the 1960s, when pro sports started to a) get integrated and b) expand more fully out of the Mid-Atlantic/New England region.

Once hip-hop got a hold of it, "swole" started being used in various ways:

It can mean literally swollen, like MOP's threat to rob you and leave "your whole shit swole up" in "Down 4 Whateva" or Mack 10's brag that his "pockets on swole like I'm fresh out parole" on "Thugz".

It's also used in the manner Clinton seemed to be using, where to "be swole" is to be upset: when someone is "all swole acting like he trynta buss" on UGK's "Touched."

But the dominant meaning, especially in the past few years, is to be extremely muscular. It's probably completely untrue (there are plenty of examples of it being used this way prior to it) but I like to think this definition entered the popular consciousness during the brief period in 1999 when Master P partnered with World Championship Wrestling to have a stable of grapplers called the No Limit Soldiers. One of the centerpieces of the stable was an incredibly steroidal young man referred to solely as "Swoll", and the announcers made great hay of both his name and physique.
